title: Artificial Intelligence as Infrastructure in 2026
overview: A talk about how artificial intelligence has changed over the past year. It covers the falling cost of models, local inference on your own hardware, and questions of access and ethics.
key_takeaways: The price per million tokens has dropped several times over, changing which tasks are worth automating.
Large models now run on a single consumer graphics card.
Local inference matters first for the privacy of personal data, not only for speed.
The cost drop carries risks for the labor market and raises the question of who benefits.

section_timecodes.title: Local inference on your own hardware

core_idea: Artificial intelligence is ceasing to be a separate product and is becoming infrastructure, like electricity or connectivity.
